title: Air Suspension Compressor Relay Circuit
shortDescription: Air suspension compressor relay control circuit malfunction.
fullDescription: DTC C1500: Air suspension compressor relay control circuit malfunction. Chassis C-codes in the C1500–C1900 range cover air suspension, electric power steering, TPMS, and adaptive damping subsystems.
safetyImpact: Chassis faults can degrade handling, ride height, or steering assist. Steering or roll-control failures should be addressed before further driving.

causes.cause: Wiring harness damage or connector corrosion
Air leak in suspension lines or air spring

symptoms: Vehicle leaning or sagging on one corner
Compressor running continuously or not at all

fixSteps.title: Scan Chassis Modules
fixSteps.instruction: Use a scan tool that supports chassis (ABS/SAS/EPS/AIR) modules to read live data and freeze frame.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Components
fixSteps.instruction: Visually inspect ride-height links, air lines, steering column, and harness connectors for damage.

fixSteps.title: Test Circuits
fixSteps.instruction: Backprobe sensor and actuator circuits for power, ground, and signal continuity per the wiring diagram.

fixSteps.title: Replace and Calibrate
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the failed component and perform required calibration (steering angle reset, ride-height calibration).

faq.q: Is it safe to drive with a chassis code?
faq.a: Steering and suspension faults can affect handling. If the warning light is red or the vehicle pulls/sags, do not drive — tow it.

faq.q: Why does the steering need calibration?
faq.a: Modern EPS and stability systems rely on a zero-point steering angle. After replacement or alignment, calibration tells the module which position is straight ahead.

faq.q: Can I DIY this?
faq.a: Inspection and basic component swaps are DIY-friendly, but calibration usually requires a scan tool with chassis support.

faq.q: Is it safe to drive with a chassis code?
